title: Governance, Risk & Regulation
subtitle: Move fast without creating unmanaged enterprise exposure
summary: Operationalize AI governance using risk tiers, lifecycle controls, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, OECD principles, privacy/security practices, and current regulation.

lessons.title: NIST AI RMF
lessons.body: Study GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE. Build governance into delivery rather than adding a compliance gate at the end. Use the GenAI profile to understand risks specific to generative systems.

lessons.title: ISO/IEC 42001 and management systems
lessons.body: Understand the logic of an AI management system: policy, accountability, objectives, risk management, controls, monitoring, auditability, and continual improvement.

lessons.title: Responsible AI principles
lessons.body: Study transparency, explainability, robustness, security, safety, accountability, human oversight, and stakeholder impact. Translate principles into engineering and business controls.

lessons.title: EU AI Act and regulatory scanning
lessons.body: Learn risk classification, transparency obligations, GPAI considerations, high-risk systems, recordkeeping, literacy, and the implementation timeline. Build a process to monitor regulatory change instead of memorizing one snapshot.

quiz.q: The strongest AI governance design is:
options: A final legal review after development
One universal approval path for every use case

quiz.q: In the NIST AI RMF, what does the MAP function help a team do?
options: Understand the system’s context, intended use, affected people, and risks
Approve a model based on one benchmark

quiz.q: A recruitment tool will be used in Toronto and Paris. What is the right governance starting point?
options: Apply one US federal rule to both offices
Assess EU AI Act role and use category, GDPR personal-data processing, and the applicable Canadian privacy regime for the actual deployments
Assume the EU AI Act replaces GDPR
Apply Canada’s federal public-service automation directive to every private employer

homework: Create an AI governance playbook with 3 risk tiers, required evidence per tier, approval roles, red-team/evaluation requirements, incident escalation, vendor review, and an AI-system registry.
regionalResources: Canada Directive on Automated Decision-Making (federal government)
Canadian privacy regulators: principles for generative AI

visual.title: Jurisdiction check for one AI use case
regions: Identify applicable federal or provincial privacy law. Public-sector automation may trigger additional directives.
Assess AI Act role and risk category. Review GDPR separately when personal data is used.
Review relevant federal, state, and sector requirements for the particular use.
visual.note: Confirm current rules and applicability with legal and privacy specialists.
